Official SingStat SSIC 9602 Industry Trend (2019–2024)

Operating revenue rose +55.5% (S$2.17B → S$3.38B) and establishments grew +33.0% (8,453 → 11,241) across Hairdressing, Barber, Beauty, Spa & Nail services (2020 not published separately).

Yearly Haircut Demand Trajectory & Population Base (2016–2026)

Because SingStat does not count individual haircuts directly, the chart pairs exact Population in Brief (2016–2026) mid-year populations with your selected cadence assumption to show the macro demand band.

Est. 2026 SG Haircuts: 52.8M
Post-2021 Demographic Rebound

Total population dropped from 5.70M (2019) to 5.45M (2021) during COVID border restrictions before climbing +13.9% to 6.21M (June 2026), directly lifting salon & barber footfall.

Super-Aged Shift (12.4% → 19.5% 65+)

Residents aged 65+ rose every year from 2016 (12.4%) to 2026 (19.5%; median age 43.6y), expanding demand for accessible HDB void-deck salons & traditional neighbourhood barbers.

Household Spend Context (HES 2023)

SingStat Household Expenditure Survey (2023) places average resident household spending at S$5,931/mo (vs. S$5,163 in 2017/18), grouping personal care under Misc. Goods & Services.

Methodological Note: Why There Are No Biological or Racial Cadence Multipliers Here

SingStat publishes resident demographics by CMIO (`Chinese 73.9% · Malay 13.5% · Indian 9.0% · Others 3.6%`), Sex & Age (Table M810011 / Population in Brief 2026) and aggregate SSIC 9602 receipts, not per-capita haircut spend by race. Trichology papers on curly-hair biomechanics also do not predict annual `S$` spend. Below, you directly control your cut frequency, gender/child ticket tier, and any verified Singapore service requirement (such as Muslimah private suites or unshorn Sikh Kesh).
